title: 1.1.23 Unit 1.1 Quiz
description: Ten multiple-choice questions on typeof, declarations, vocabulary and the class style guide. Checked instantly.

questions.question: What does `typeof "42"` give you?
options: "number"
"string"
"object"
questions.explanation: The quotes make it a string, whatever is inside them. `typeof 42` without quotes is "number".

questions.question: What does `typeof undefined` give you?
options: "undefined"
"object"
"null"
An error
questions.explanation: It answers "undefined". That is the one case where the type name and the value name are the same word.

questions.question: What does `typeof null` give you?
options: "null"
"undefined"
"object"
"empty"
questions.explanation: It answers "object" — which is wrong, and is a bug in the language from 1995 that was never fixed because fixing it would break existing sites.

questions.question: What is wrong with `let 2cool = true;`?
options: true has to be in quotes
A variable name cannot start with a digit
You have to use const for a boolean
Nothing — it is valid
questions.explanation: Names may contain digits but cannot start with one. `let cool2 = true;` is fine.

questions.question: What is wrong with `const userName;`?
options: const names must be in capitals
userName is a reserved word
A const must be given its value on the line that declares it, because it can never be reassigned
Nothing — it is valid
questions.explanation: A const gets exactly one chance to be given a value, and that is at declaration. If you need to fill it in later, use let.

questions.question: What is wrong with `let user-name = "Al";`?
options: The hyphen is read as a minus sign, so this is not a valid name
The value needs to be in single quotes
Names cannot contain more than one word
Nothing — it is valid
questions.explanation: JavaScript sees `user - name`, a subtraction. Join the words with camelCase instead: `let userName = "Al";`

questions.question: What is a constant?
options: A variable whose value can never be changed once it is set
A variable that holds a number
A variable that every part of the program can see
A value that is written directly into the code
questions.explanation: A constant is declared with const and cannot be reassigned. Reach for it whenever a value is not meant to move.

questions.question: What is a data type?
options: The name you give a variable
The kind of value something is — text, a number, true/false, and so on
The amount of memory a program uses
A comment describing what a variable is for
questions.explanation: The type is what kind of thing the value is, which decides what you can do with it — you can add two numbers, but adding two booleans is not meaningful.

questions.question: What does the class style guide say is wrong with `let x=5`?
options: Nothing — it runs, so it is fine
It needs spaces around the = and a semicolon at the end, and x is a name that says nothing
let should be const
5 needs to be in quotes
questions.explanation: It runs, but three things break the guide at once: no spaces around the operator, no semicolon, and a single-letter name.

questions.question: What does the class style guide say is wrong with `let UserName = "Al";`?
options: Variable names cannot contain capital letters
The name is too long
Variables use camelCase, so the first letter should be lower case — userName
It should be a const
questions.explanation: camelCase means the first word is lower case and later words are capitalised. A capitalised first letter is by convention reserved for classes, which you meet in Chapter 5.
